description.narrative: To design and develop plant-based natural product innovations using Croton seed oil and the by-products from its extraction for sustainable, organic agriculture in Kenya that reduces farmer reliance on synthetic chemical pesticides and increases revenue for the farmers and the KTP business partner.

To design and develop plant-based natural product innovations using Croton seed oil and the by-products from its extraction for sustainable, organic agriculture in Kenya that reduces farmer reliance on synthetic chemical pesticides and increases revenue for the farmers and the KTP business partner. Innovation area – Pest control Croton oil is extracted as a biofuel from Croton seeds and remains EFKs primary source of revenue. However, it is our strategic aim to commercialise Croton seed oil and by-products of its extraction into a wider product range, especially sustainable pest control. African farming is reliant on synthetic pesticides that have negative environmental and health impacts, and limit export potential to EU owing to residue restrictions (2009 EU Sustainable Use Directive). In response, EFKs vision is to increase revenue using Croton for eco-friendly and sustainable agriculture. Routes to diversifying our portfolio include a) extracts from seed kernels as organic pesticides and plant growth boosters b) use of the oil in plant-based organic pesticide formulations. However, the evidence on efficacy remains anecdotal at this stage and requires scientific validation to be able to correctly develop and market these products. EFK currently lack the expertise for this validation. ODA – This project has several wider benefits. By helping EFK grow its business, this project will benefit EFK’s croton collector network by increasing farmer income. If EFK is able to scale as projected to collect 7000 tons per year, this injects over £1.0M of additional income to smallholder farmers. Also, by increasing its market share for organic agricultural products, EFKs products will help revitalize farms and aid farmers in engaging in climate-smart agricultural practices. One of the current barriers to proper fertilizer and pesticide use is that farmers lack the correct training to correctly utilize products often resulting in hazardous use, especially with chemical pesticides. This project will result in smallholder farmers engaging in safe usage of organic products benefitting both themselves and the consumers of their produce. Finally, Kenya’s agricultural sector is over-reliant on foreign imports. The new croton-pyrethrum product will result in a completed new and organic product that is tied to key Kenyan natural resources. Kenya was once the biggest producer of high quality pyrethrum. This project will help engage regrowing that industry as it continues to develop the croton as new supply chain. This project supports the growth and scale of a local Kenya organization in creating products that have direct local benefits.
